faq.q: What does it mean to wear a mask to hide your true self?
faq.a: It means showing a safer, more acceptable version of yourself while keeping your real thoughts, feelings, or needs out of sight. The mask is usually an edit rather than an outright lie.

faq.q: Why do people hide their true selves?
faq.a: Most masks grow out of fear of rejection, judgment, or conflict. They often start in childhood or at work as a sensible way to stay safe or accepted.

faq.q: Is wearing a social mask always bad?
faq.a: No. Some social polish is kind and appropriate. It becomes a problem when the mask never comes off, even with the people closest to you or when you're alone.

faq.q: What are signs I'm masking too much?
faq.a: Common signs include feeling drained after social time, rehearsing conversations, saying yes while meaning no, and feeling that compliments describe someone you're performing.

faq.q: How can I stop hiding who I really am?
faq.a: Start by noticing when you reach for the mask, then name what's underneath in private. From there, share one honest sentence with one safe person and build slowly.

faq.q: What is the difference between authenticity and oversharing?
faq.a: Authenticity means what you share is true. Oversharing means sharing everything with everyone, which can become its own kind of performance.
